newsitem.title: UK: UK regulator reaches deal with Vodafone.
newsitem.headline: UK regulator reaches deal with Vodafone.

text.p: Britain's Office of Fair Trading said on Thursday it withdrew the threat of possible legal action against Vodafone Group Plc after the phone firm agreed to make changes to its contracts with consumers.

The competition watchdog said Vodafone agreed among other things to drop its disconnection charge of 50 stg plus value-added tax (VAT) and would also reduce its requirement for termination notices to one month from 90 days.
The changes would affect all Vodafone consumer contracts made on or after July 1, 1995.

The OFT said discussions were continuing with eight other airtime suppliers, including Astec Communications, British Telecom, Call Connections, One 2 One, Motorola Tel-co, Orange Personal Communications, Peoples Phone Co, and UniqueAir. "The other airtime suppliers have offered further changes, but none has yet gone far enough to satisfy me that all unfair terms have been removed from their contracts," director general of fair trading John Bridgeman said in a statement.
